features.title: Clause roles and finite predicates
features.scope_note: Identify complete clauses, finite predicate, expressed/understood subject and governed complements by morphology, agreement and frame; order is corroboration, not the sole criterion.

features.title: Main-clause fronting
features.scope_note: Subject-initial and fronted main clauses; second constituent is not second written word. Finite-second is an evidenced tendency, with actual exceptions; no automatic transformation.

features.title: Pronoun position and limits
features.scope_note: A subject pronoun may precede the finite verb after a fronted adverbial: exact Æfter ðon hē underðēodde. Neither pronouns nor fronting impose an exceptionless placement rule.

features.title: Sustained reference and ambiguity
features.scope_note: Recover antecedents through agreement, syntax, discourse and meaning. Masculine sang can be referred to by hē/hine; identical masculine candidates can remain ambiguous. Do not choose nearest noun mechanically.

features.title: Coordination and predicate recovery
features.scope_note: Recover a shared subject or repeated lexical predicate only where the clauses support it. Restore finite agreement with the second expressed subject: singular wæs becomes plural wǣron. Cook134.1–2 independently has singular cymð and omitted plural coming.

features.title: Person in reported and quoted speech
features.scope_note: Within direct quotation, first and second person refer to current speaker and addressees. In indirect report, contextual third-person reference can be explicit or ambiguous; mood does not identify the antecedent.

features.title: Long-sentence analysis
features.scope_note: Find boundaries and finite predicates before resolving reference; keep embedded clauses and coordinated material separate; return to apposition and source notes where necessary.

features.title: Long fronting in the source
features.scope_note: Recognition only with explicit help: Cook152.8–9 Ðā stefne and ðone sang are accusatives governed by embedded gehīerde, as note8 says. Do not teach them as ordinary objects of cwæð or license free long extraction.

features.title: Dependent clause order
features.scope_note: Dependent finite predicates often occur late/end, but need not be last. Cook25.7 expressly asks verb last for that item; this is a target constraint, not a general validity test.

features.title: Correlative and homographic clause markers
features.scope_note: Reuse taught temporal/causal relatives and correlatives. Distinguish temporal conjunction ðā, main adverb ðā, and demonstrative/article ðā by construction, agreement and context; paired when/then can clarify. No universal inversion diagnostic.

features.title: Negation and questions in clause analysis
features.scope_note: Reuse ne plus finite, negative concord, interrogative-word and finite-initial yes/no questions; existing forms/moods only. This reinforces earlier systems and does not silently add contracted negative copulas.

features.scope_note: Complete present/past participle base pair. Base formation is productive; only the past base is used in taught uninflected predicative passives. No attributive participle declension or independent use of every present participle is licensed.

features.description: sume dæge; hwæthwugu swilces; ūte
features.scope_note: Sume dæge is a time expression, “one day”; sume is the instrumental form. Hwæthwugu means “something”; swilces is neuter genitive, “of this kind.” Ūte means “outside.”
features.grammar_owner_reconciliation: Exact source application; productive general grammar milestones are separate Unit 13 grammar records.

features.description: ciricean
features.scope_note: Ciricean is the source genitive or dative spelling corresponding to productive cirican: genitive when dependent on roof or window, dative after tō or locative in. The same noun can name either the community church or Chad’s oratory; context and Cook’s note distinguish the buildings.
features.grammar_owner_reconciliation: Exact source application; productive general grammar milestones are separate Unit 13 grammar records.

features.description: gelōmlice; āna; in bēcrǣdinge / in gebedum geornfull
features.scope_note: Gelōmlice means “often”; āna, “alone.” Bēcrǣdinge means “reading books”; gebedum is dative plural, “prayers”; geornfull here means “occupied” or “intent.” In governs the dative in these expressions.
features.grammar_owner_reconciliation: Exact source application; productive general grammar milestones are separate Unit 13 grammar records.

features.description: gehīerde; sęmninga; swā-swā; ęft æfter ðon
features.scope_note: Gehīerde is prefixed “heard.” Sęmninga means “suddenly”; swā-swā, “just as”; ęft, “again” or “afterwards” as the context requires. Æfter ðon means “after that”; ðon is the source dative demonstrative variant.
features.grammar_owner_reconciliation: Exact source application; productive general grammar milestones are separate Unit 13 grammar records.

features.description: swētestan / fægerestan stefne; singendra and blissiendra; oð; āstīgan
features.scope_note: Stefne is accusative feminine singular, “voice.” Fægerestan means “most beautiful,” agreeing with stefne. Singendra and blissiendra are genitive plural participles used substantivally, “of people singing and rejoicing.” Oð means “as far as.” Āstīgan here means “descend.”
features.grammar_owner_reconciliation: Exact source application; productive general grammar milestones are separate Unit 13 grammar records.

features.description: Ðā stefne and ðone sang … gehīerde
features.scope_note: The initial accusative objects belong with the later gehīerde inside the reported clause. Cwæð introduces the report. Ǣrest means “first.” Do not turn the fronted accusatives into subjects.
features.grammar_owner_reconciliation: Exact source application; productive general grammar milestones are separate Unit 13 grammar records.

features.description: ēastsūðdǣle; hēanesse; winterlican sunnan ūpganges; ðanan
features.scope_note: Ēastsūðdǣle means “southeastern part”; hēanesse, “height”; winterlican, “winter,” agrees with genitive sunnan; ūpganges means “rising.” Ðanan means “from there.”
features.grammar_owner_reconciliation: Exact source application; productive general grammar milestones are separate Unit 13 grammar records.

features.description: styccemǣlum; nēalǣcton; oð-ðæt hē becōm
features.scope_note: Styccemǣlum means “little by little.” Nēalǣcton is third plural: the voice and song approached. Oð-ðæt means “until.” Becōm means “arrived”; the following singular reference is explained by Cook’s note 9a.
features.grammar_owner_reconciliation: Exact source application; productive general grammar milestones are separate Unit 13 grammar records.

features.description: ðæcean … ðe … in
features.scope_note: Ðæcean is dative singular, “roof.” The relative ðe is governed by the later in, “in which”; the preposition follows its relative.
features.grammar_owner_reconciliation: Exact source application; productive general grammar milestones are separate Unit 13 grammar records.

features.description: ingangende; eall; in ymbhwyrfte ymbsealde
features.scope_note: Ingangende is a present participle, “entering.” Eall is accusative neuter singular, “everything.” Gefylde means “filled.” In ymbhwyrfte means “all around”; ymbsealde means “surrounded.” These continue the description of the song.
features.grammar_owner_reconciliation: Exact source application; productive general grammar milestones are separate Unit 13 grammar records.

features.description: geornlice; his mōd āðęnede in …
features.scope_note: Geornlice means “attentively.” Mōd is “mind”; āðęnede is “directed/stretched.” The whole attention expression means to direct one’s mind or attention to something; in has the accusative here.
features.grammar_owner_reconciliation: Exact source application; productive general grammar milestones are separate Unit 13 grammar records.

features.description: ęft swā-swā healfre tīde fæce
features.scope_note: Here swā-swā means “about,” not “just as.” Healfre tīde is genitive, “of half an hour”; fæce is dative of the interval after which the event occurs. The hour sense of tīde is supplied separately.
features.grammar_owner_reconciliation: Exact source application; productive general grammar milestones are separate Unit 13 grammar records.

features.description: ūpāstīgan; blissesang; ðȳ ilcan wege; unasęcgendre swētnesse; ęfthweorfan
features.scope_note: Ūpāstīgan means “rise up”; blissesang, “song of joy.” Ðȳ ilcan wege is the supported route expression, “by the same way”; ǣr means “previously.” Unasęcgendre swētnesse means “with indescribable sweetness” after mid. Ęfthweorfan means “return.” The two infinitives depend on heard.
features.grammar_owner_reconciliation: Exact source application; productive general grammar milestones are separate Unit 13 grammar records.

features.description: wunode; sum fæc tīde; wundriende and wafiende
features.scope_note: Wunode means “remained”; ðǣr, “there.” Sum fæc tīde is an accusative duration expression, “for a while.” Wundriende and wafiende are uninflected participles describing the observer as wondering and amazed.
features.grammar_owner_reconciliation: Exact source application; productive general grammar milestones are separate Unit 13 grammar records.

features.description: mid behygdigum mōde; ðōhte and smēade; hwæt … bēon sceolden
features.scope_note: Behygdigum mōde means “with an attentive mind.” Ðōhte and smēade mean “thought” and “pondered.” The embedded question asks what the things might be or mean; sceolden is preterite subjunctive plural, with infinitive bēon.
features.grammar_owner_reconciliation: Exact source application; productive general grammar milestones are separate Unit 13 grammar records.

features.description: ontȳnde; ēagðȳrel; handa; slōg tācen; swā-swā; gewuna
features.scope_note: Ontȳnde means “opened.” Handa is the source dative form of hand. Slōg tācen means “made a signal,” literally “struck a sign.” Swā-swā means “just as.” Gewuna means “custom” or “habit.”
features.grammar_owner_reconciliation: Exact source application; productive general grammar milestones are separate Unit 13 grammar records.

features.description: gif hwilc mann … wǣre; ðæt … ēode; in; sōna
features.scope_note: Hwilc mann here means “anyone.” Wǣre is preterite subjunctive in the habitual condition. The ðæt clause states the content or purpose of the signal. In is the adverb “in”; sōna means “immediately.”
features.grammar_owner_reconciliation: Exact source application; productive general grammar milestones are separate Unit 13 grammar records.

features.description: Cwæð … him tō; Gang; hāt; ēac swilce mid wes
features.scope_note: The separated him … tō identifies the person addressed. Gang means “go” (singular imperative); hraðe, “quickly.” Hāt is singular “command/tell,” with an accusative subject and infinitive. Hider means “hither/here.” Ēac swilce means “also”; mid is adverbial “with them”; wes is singular “be.”
features.grammar_owner_reconciliation: Exact source application; productive general grammar milestones are separate Unit 13 grammar records.

features.description: Unordered local material: Gode, dative recipient; gōdes willan, the bounded quality expression “of good will”; hēanessum, dative plural “heights”; sibb, nominative “peace”; sīe, optative “be”; wuldor, nominative “glory.” Supply the complete doxological construction: dative recipient with nominative glory, and an understood parallel wish of peace for the men described. This formula does not establish unrestricted genitive-quality syntax.

features.description: Feallan is the supplied plain infinitive “fall.” Use the already taught gesēon + accusative actor + plain infinitive construction.
features.scope_note: Visible bounded help; independent recall is not assessed.

features.description: Ðǣra is the supplied genitive plural variant corresponding to ordinary ðāra. It agrees with the plural trees.
features.scope_note: Visible bounded help; independent recall is not assessed.

features.description: Unordered local material: cweðendra, “of people saying”; getæl, “number/company”; hęriendra, “of people praising”; heofonlices weorodes, “of a heavenly host”; sęmninga, “suddenly.” The genitive plural participles are substantival and supported in this collective-number formula. Identify their functions with this help; do not independently derive a participle paradigm.

features.description: Hwæthwega means “something” and takes the supplied partitive expression swilces, “of this kind.” The reading’s different exact hwæthwugu spelling remains separately recorded.
features.scope_note: Visible bounded help; independent recall is not assessed.

features.description: The address “you of little faith” is locally supplied as gē lȳtles gelēafan. Lȳtles gelēafan is the bounded genitive quality expression; no general productive rule is inferred.
features.scope_note: Visible bounded help; independent recall is not assessed.

features.description: Supply micle, instrumental neuter singular used adverbially before mā, for “much more.” Recognition of that cell elsewhere does not establish independent productive recall here.

features.description: Supply Æðelðrȳð as the nominative personal name and Eastęngla as the genitive plural “of the East Anglians.” No productive proper-name system is assigned.
features.scope_note: Visible bounded help; independent recall is not assessed.

features.description: Sē is the retained long source spelling of the nominative masculine singular demonstrative/relative. The ordinary short se remains a valid taught alternative; the added quantity is not an independent recall target.
features.scope_note: Visible bounded help; independent recall is not assessed.

features.description: For the local placement phrase, use tō with dative wyrttruman and a genitive plural trees phrase. The phrase denotes placement at/to the root; it does not create a general static tō rule.
features.scope_note: Visible bounded help; independent recall is not assessed.

features.description: For this taking action, the bounded phrase on his hand means “into his hand,” with accusative hand. This is a declared composition applying Cook’s qualified directional use of on and the ordinary sense of niman; it is not an attested Old English quotation or a general productive niman-plus-goal rule. A static dative “in his hand” is a defensible alternative construal.
features.scope_note: Visible bounded help; independent recall is not assessed.

features.description: Tō-morgen means “tomorrow” and is supplied as one invariant temporal expression.
features.scope_note: Visible bounded help; independent recall is not assessed.

features.description: In the local wonder question, hit anticipates the following circumstance. Wundor is a nominal predicate; ðēah introduces the conceded circumstance with a preterite subjunctive. An admitted fact is compatible with this subjunctive.
features.scope_note: Visible bounded help; independent recall is not assessed.

features.description: Uncontracted ne eom is available for “I am not.” The bounded worthy-content construction uses a present subjunctive; under in the entry phrase takes an accusative roof. No negative-copula contraction is required.
features.scope_note: Visible bounded help; independent recall is not assessed.

features.description: Cook43: masculine singular N/A stem, G -es, D -e; plural N/A -as, G -a, D -um. Retain both vowels in bisceop, ofen and æcer; their dictionary class supplies no license for arbitrary syncope.

features.description: Cook44: replace citation -e before endings; singular N/A and D have -e. Gefērscipe follows the explicitly named -scipe class.

features.description: Cook47: strong neuter singular N/A citation form, G -es, D -e; plural G -a, D -um. Heavy monosyllables have zero N/A plural. For disyllables Cook47.1 allows zero or -u; select mynstru and ēagðȳrlu. Cook47.1 explicitly selects usual wundor, not an invented plural in -as.

features.description: Cook43.4 and47.6: a short second vowel is normally lost before a vowel ending when the preceding stem syllable is heavy. Thus mynster → mynstr-, ēagðȳrel → ēagðȳrl-, wundor → wundr-. The uninflected citation form remains; do not extend syncope to ofen, æcer or bisceop.
features.scope_note: The full recorded nominal systems retain individual sense/number limits; distinct instrumental reference cells create no independent instrumental use.

features.description: Cook51b: long feminine singular N citation, G/D/A -e; plural N/A -a (also -e), G -a, D -um. Æx keeps æ: the single-consonant short-masculine æ/a alternation does not apply to this feminine cluster stem. Synn is the selected full citation variant of Cook syn(n).
features.scope_note: The full recorded nominal systems retain individual sense/number limits; distinct instrumental reference cells create no independent instrumental use.

features.description: Cook51.5: -nes doubles s before inflectional endings and retains e. Cook51.3: -ung has the ordinary feminine endings, with -a also attested in singular oblique cases; select -e consistently. Abstract plural cells are reference forms; the assigned abstract sense is singular.
features.scope_note: The full recorded nominal systems retain individual sense/number limits; distinct instrumental reference cells create no independent instrumental use.

features.description: Cook53: masculine N singular -a, all other singular cases and N/A plural -an; G plural -ena, D plural -um. Feminine citation -e, otherwise the same selected pattern. Productive cirican replaces citation -e; retain the source-only ciricean spelling separately.
features.scope_note: The full recorded nominal systems retain individual sense/number limits; distinct instrumental reference cells create no independent instrumental use.

features.description: Cook46.1 and52.2, checked against Wright415: brōðor, mōdor, dohtor have unchanged singular N/G/A; D singular brēðer, mēder, dehter. Selected N/A plural brōðor, mōdru, dohtor; G plural brōðra, mōdra, dohtra; D plural brōðrum, mōdrum, dohtrum. Dohtor has short o. Plurals brōðru, mōdra and dohtru/dohtra are documented alternatives. Wright thorn is declared normalized to Cook eth in the derived course paradigm.
features.scope_note: The full recorded nominal systems retain individual sense/number limits; distinct instrumental reference cells create no independent instrumental use.

features.description: Cook52.1: burg has selected G/D singular and N/A plural byrig; singular N/A burg, plural G burga and D burgum. Burge is an accepted G singular variant.
features.scope_note: The full recorded nominal systems retain individual sense/number limits; distinct instrumental reference cells create no independent instrumental use.

features.description: Cook46.3: frēond is the explicitly named companion of fēond. Reuse the established complete fēond model, replacing fēond-/fīend with frēond-/frīend. Selected D singular frēonde, N/A plural frīend, G plural frēonda, D plural frēondum. Do not infer genitive frēondra from the ordinary -end participle pattern.
features.scope_note: The full recorded nominal systems retain individual sense/number limits; distinct instrumental reference cells create no independent instrumental use.

features.description: Cook57–59: complete strong NGDA singular/plural in all three genders; masculine/neuter singular instrumental -e shown for reference. Long monosyllables lose the short-class -u in feminine N singular and neuter N/A plural. Adjectives in -e retain it only without another ending, otherwise replace it; their feminine N singular and neuter N/A plural end in -u.
features.scope_note: The full recorded nominal systems retain individual sense/number limits; distinct instrumental reference cells create no independent instrumental use.

features.description: Cook60: weak masculine N singular -a, feminine N singular and neuter N/A singular -e, other singular cases and plural N/A -an; G plural -ra (also -ena), D plural -um. The table establishes forms, not unrestricted article or comparison syntax.
features.scope_note: The full recorded nominal systems retain individual sense/number limits; distinct instrumental reference cells create no independent instrumental use.

features.description: Cook57.3 explicitly gives hālig, not hāl(i)gu, for feminine N singular and neuter N/A plural. Select syncope hālg- before vowel endings, retaining hālig- before -ne, -re, -ra. Hęfig retains its medial vowel after the light first syllable; do not create hęfges.
features.scope_note: The full recorded nominal systems retain individual sense/number limits; distinct instrumental reference cells create no independent instrumental use.

features.description: Cook63: regular comparative -ra and superlative -ost/-est; remove citation -e. Swētra is rule-derived from swēte; exact swētestan is independently present in the assigned source. Comparatives have weak inflection only; superlatives can use strong and weak inflection. Wright §259.3 simplifies a doubled consonant after another consonant: swētr- + -ra gives selected genitive plural swētra, not mechanically assembled swētrra. This is a rule-derived cell, not a separately attested quotation. No strong comparative table is generated.
features.scope_note: The full recorded nominal systems retain individual sense/number limits; distinct instrumental reference cells create no independent instrumental use.

teaching_records.text: Sume dæge is a time expression, “one day”; sume is the instrumental form. Hwæthwugu means “something”; swilces is neuter genitive, “of this kind.” Ūte means “outside.”

Ciricean is the source genitive or dative spelling corresponding to productive cirican: genitive when dependent on roof or window, dative after tō or locative in. The same noun can name either the community church or Chad’s oratory; context and Cook’s note distinguish the buildings.
Gelōmlice means “often”; āna, “alone.” Bēcrǣdinge means “reading books”; gebedum is dative plural, “prayers”; geornfull here means “occupied” or “intent.” In governs the dative in these expressions.

Gehīerde is prefixed “heard.” Sęmninga means “suddenly”; swā-swā, “just as”; ęft, “again” or “afterwards” as the context requires. Æfter ðon means “after that”; ðon is the source dative demonstrative variant.

Stefne is accusative feminine singular, “voice.” Fægerestan means “most beautiful,” agreeing with stefne. Singendra and blissiendra are genitive plural participles used substantivally, “of people singing and rejoicing.” Oð means “as far as.” Āstīgan here means “descend.”
The initial accusative objects belong with the later gehīerde inside the reported clause. Cwæð introduces the report. Ǣrest means “first.” Do not turn the fronted accusatives into subjects.
Ēastsūðdǣle means “southeastern part”; hēanesse, “height”; winterlican, “winter,” agrees with genitive sunnan; ūpganges means “rising.” Ðanan means “from there.”

Styccemǣlum means “little by little.” Nēalǣcton is third plural: the voice and song approached. Oð-ðæt means “until.” Becōm means “arrived”; the following singular reference is explained by Cook’s note 9a.
Ðæcean is dative singular, “roof.” The relative ðe is governed by the later in, “in which”; the preposition follows its relative.

Ingangende is a present participle, “entering.” Eall is accusative neuter singular, “everything.” Gefylde means “filled.” In ymbhwyrfte means “all around”; ymbsealde means “surrounded.” These continue the description of the song.
Geornlice means “attentively.” Mōd is “mind”; āðęnede is “directed/stretched.” The whole attention expression means to direct one’s mind or attention to something; in has the accusative here.
Here swā-swā means “about,” not “just as.” Healfre tīde is genitive, “of half an hour”; fæce is dative of the interval after which the event occurs. The hour sense of tīde is supplied separately.

Ūpāstīgan means “rise up”; blissesang, “song of joy.” Ðȳ ilcan wege is the supported route expression, “by the same way”; ǣr means “previously.” Unasęcgendre swētnesse means “with indescribable sweetness” after mid. Ęfthweorfan means “return.” The two infinitives depend on heard.

Wunode means “remained”; ðǣr, “there.” Sum fæc tīde is an accusative duration expression, “for a while.” Wundriende and wafiende are uninflected participles describing the observer as wondering and amazed.

Behygdigum mōde means “with an attentive mind.” Ðōhte and smēade mean “thought” and “pondered.” The embedded question asks what the things might be or mean; sceolden is preterite subjunctive plural, with infinitive bēon.
Ontȳnde means “opened.” Handa is the source dative form of hand. Slōg tācen means “made a signal,” literally “struck a sign.” Swā-swā means “just as.” Gewuna means “custom” or “habit.”
Hwilc mann here means “anyone.” Wǣre is preterite subjunctive in the habitual condition. The ðæt clause states the content or purpose of the signal. In is the adverb “in”; sōna means “immediately.”

The separated him … tō identifies the person addressed. Gang means “go” (singular imperative); hraðe, “quickly.” Hāt is singular “command/tell,” with an accusative subject and infinitive. Hider means “hither/here.” Ēac swilce means “also”; mid is adverbial “with them”; wes is singular “be.”
Supply Æðelðrȳð as the nominative personal name and Eastęngla as the genitive plural “of the East Anglians.” No productive proper-name system is assigned.

Sē is the retained long source spelling of the nominative masculine singular demonstrative/relative. The ordinary short se remains a valid taught alternative; the added quantity is not an independent recall target.
Ðǣra is the supplied genitive plural variant corresponding to ordinary ðāra. It agrees with the plural trees.
For the local placement phrase, use tō with dative wyrttruman and a genitive plural trees phrase. The phrase denotes placement at/to the root; it does not create a general static tō rule.

For this taking action, the bounded phrase on his hand means “into his hand,” with accusative hand. This is a declared composition applying Cook’s qualified directional use of on and the ordinary sense of niman; it is not an attested Old English quotation or a general productive niman-plus-goal rule. A static dative “in his hand” is a defensible alternative construal.
Feallan is the supplied plain infinitive “fall.” Use the already taught gesēon + accusative actor + plain infinitive construction.

Uncontracted ne eom is available for “I am not.” The bounded worthy-content construction uses a present subjunctive; under in the entry phrase takes an accusative roof. No negative-copula contraction is required.
Supply micle, instrumental neuter singular used adverbially before mā, for “much more.” Recognition of that cell elsewhere does not establish independent productive recall here.
Tō-morgen means “tomorrow” and is supplied as one invariant temporal expression.
The address “you of little faith” is locally supplied as gē lȳtles gelēafan. Lȳtles gelēafan is the bounded genitive quality expression; no general productive rule is inferred.

In the local wonder question, hit anticipates the following circumstance. Wundor is a nominal predicate; ðēah introduces the conceded circumstance with a preterite subjunctive. An admitted fact is compatible with this subjunctive.
Hwæthwega means “something” and takes the supplied partitive expression swilces, “of this kind.” The reading’s different exact hwæthwugu spelling remains separately recorded.

Unordered local material: cweðendra, “of people saying”; getæl, “number/company”; hęriendra, “of people praising”; heofonlices weorodes, “of a heavenly host”; sęmninga, “suddenly.” The genitive plural participles are substantival and supported in this collective-number formula. Identify their functions with this help; do not independently derive a participle paradigm.

Unordered local material: Gode, dative recipient; gōdes willan, the bounded quality expression “of good will”; hēanessum, dative plural “heights”; sibb, nominative “peace”; sīe, optative “be”; wuldor, nominative “glory.” Supply the complete doxological construction: dative recipient with nominative glory, and an understood parallel wish of peace for the men described. This formula does not establish unrestricted genitive-quality syntax.

Citation support: forceorfan, forcearf, forcurfon, forcorfen. These four printed parts identify the present, preterite singular, preterite plural and past participle stems. Keep the row visible; only the separately assigned systems and uses are recall targets.

This complete fragment is supplied as corroborative evidence outside the assigned continuous reading. Æfter ðon means after that; hē is Chad; underðēodde means added to his speech (Cook note13: Latin subjunxit). Identify its order only; no independent translation or lexical recall is required. The fronted temporal phrase is followed by subject pronoun, then finite verb.

exact_source_lines.text: Ðā hē ðā sume dæge hwæthwugu swilces ūte dyde,
and his gefēran tō byrig tō ciricean ēodon, swā hīe gelōm-
lice dydon, and se bisceop, āna in ðǣre ciricean, oððe in
bēcrǣdinge oððe in gebedum geornfull wæs, ðā gehīerde
hē sęmninga, swā-swā hē ęft æfter ðon sægde, ðā swēt-
estan stefne and ðā fægerestan, singendra and blis-
siendra, of heofonum oð eorðan āstīgan. Ðā stefne and
ðone sang hē cwæð ðæt hē ǣrest gehīerde fram ēast-
sūðdǣle heofones, ðæt is fram hēanesse ðǣre winterlican
sunnan ūpganges; and ðanan tō him styccemǣlum nēa-
lǣcton, oð-ðæt hē becōm tō ðæcean ðǣre ciricean ðe se
bisceop in wæs; and, ingangende, eall gefylde, and in
ymbhwyrfte ymbsealde. And hē ðā geornlice his mōd
āðęnede in ðā ðing ðe hē gehīerde. Ðā gehīerde hē
ęft swā-swā healfre tīde fæce, of hrōfe ðǣre ilcan
ciricean ūpāstīgan ðone ilcan blissesang, and, ðȳ ilcan
wege ðe hē ǣr cōm, ūp oð heofonas mid unasęcgendre
swētnesse ęfthweorfan.
Ðā wunode hē ðǣr sum fæc tīde, wundriende and
wafiende; and mid behygdigum mōde ðōhte and smēade
hwæt ðā ðing bēon sceolden. Ðā ontȳnde se bisceop ðæt
ēagðȳrel ðǣre ciricean, and mid his handa slōg tācen,
swā-swā his gewuna wæs gif hwilc mann ūte wǣre, ðæt
hē in tō him ēode. Ðā ēode hē sōna in tō him. Cwæð
hē, se bisceop, him tō: “Gang hraðe tō ciricean, and
hāt ūre seofon brōðor hider tō mē cuman; and ðū ēac
swilce mid wes.”

readings.context_only: Owini had left a court household to live and work at Chad’s monastery. While the other brothers studied inside, he did needed work outside. Chad was alone in the local oratory; the companions had gone to the community church. This English orientation is new teaching material, based on the immediately preceding Cook150–152.2 and original note152.5.
readings.unassigned_continuation: The bishop’s exhortation, declaration of his approaching death, later conversation and death follow after153.9. They were inspected to choose the boundary and are not assigned by this span.

audited_inflection_rules.text: Cook43: masculine singular N/A stem, G -es, D -e; plural N/A -as, G -a, D -um. Retain both vowels in bisceop, ofen and æcer; their dictionary class supplies no license for arbitrary syncope.
Cook44: replace citation -e before endings; singular N/A and D have -e. Gefērscipe follows the explicitly named -scipe class.

Cook47: strong neuter singular N/A citation form, G -es, D -e; plural G -a, D -um. Heavy monosyllables have zero N/A plural. For disyllables Cook47.1 allows zero or -u; select mynstru and ēagðȳrlu. Cook47.1 explicitly selects usual wundor, not an invented plural in -as.

Cook43.4 and47.6: a short second vowel is normally lost before a vowel ending when the preceding stem syllable is heavy. Thus mynster → mynstr-, ēagðȳrel → ēagðȳrl-, wundor → wundr-. The uninflected citation form remains; do not extend syncope to ofen, æcer or bisceop.

Cook51b: long feminine singular N citation, G/D/A -e; plural N/A -a (also -e), G -a, D -um. Æx keeps æ: the single-consonant short-masculine æ/a alternation does not apply to this feminine cluster stem. Synn is the selected full citation variant of Cook syn(n).

Cook51.5: -nes doubles s before inflectional endings and retains e. Cook51.3: -ung has the ordinary feminine endings, with -a also attested in singular oblique cases; select -e consistently. Abstract plural cells are reference forms; the assigned abstract sense is singular.

Cook53: masculine N singular -a, all other singular cases and N/A plural -an; G plural -ena, D plural -um. Feminine citation -e, otherwise the same selected pattern. Productive cirican replaces citation -e; retain the source-only ciricean spelling separately.

Cook46.1 and52.2, checked against Wright415: brōðor, mōdor, dohtor have unchanged singular N/G/A; D singular brēðer, mēder, dehter. Selected N/A plural brōðor, mōdru, dohtor; G plural brōðra, mōdra, dohtra; D plural brōðrum, mōdrum, dohtrum. Dohtor has short o. Plurals brōðru, mōdra and dohtru/dohtra are documented alternatives. Wright thorn is declared normalized to Cook eth in the derived course paradigm.
Cook52.1: burg has selected G/D singular and N/A plural byrig; singular N/A burg, plural G burga and D burgum. Burge is an accepted G singular variant.

Cook46.3: frēond is the explicitly named companion of fēond. Reuse the established complete fēond model, replacing fēond-/fīend with frēond-/frīend. Selected D singular frēonde, N/A plural frīend, G plural frēonda, D plural frēondum. Do not infer genitive frēondra from the ordinary -end participle pattern.

Cook57–59: complete strong NGDA singular/plural in all three genders; masculine/neuter singular instrumental -e shown for reference. Long monosyllables lose the short-class -u in feminine N singular and neuter N/A plural. Adjectives in -e retain it only without another ending, otherwise replace it; their feminine N singular and neuter N/A plural end in -u.

Cook60: weak masculine N singular -a, feminine N singular and neuter N/A singular -e, other singular cases and plural N/A -an; G plural -ra (also -ena), D plural -um. The table establishes forms, not unrestricted article or comparison syntax.

Cook57.3 explicitly gives hālig, not hāl(i)gu, for feminine N singular and neuter N/A plural. Select syncope hālg- before vowel endings, retaining hālig- before -ne, -re, -ra. Hęfig retains its medial vowel after the light first syllable; do not create hęfges.

Cook63: regular comparative -ra and superlative -ost/-est; remove citation -e. Swētra is rule-derived from swēte; exact swētestan is independently present in the assigned source. Comparatives have weak inflection only; superlatives can use strong and weak inflection. Wright §259.3 simplifies a doubled consonant after another consonant: swētr- + -ra gives selected genitive plural swētra, not mechanically assembled swētrra. This is a rule-derived cell, not a separately attested quotation. No strong comparative table is generated.

audited_inflection_rules.statement: Selected long-form weak II: -ie, -ast, -að, -iað; preterite -ode, -odest, -ode, -odon. Infinitive -ian, inflected -ianne, present participle -iende, past -od. Alternative -ige/-ade formations remain outside this selected system.
Weak I has selected present stems and dental preterite; syncope and consonant outcomes are stated per lexical row. Full singular/plural indicative endings follow §117.

The selected āstręccean system has geminate/ungeminated present alternation and unmutated preterite āstreahte. Past is not mechanically generated from the mutated infinitive. Source154 verifies āstreahte; §114 supports the lexical class.

Strong III four stems govern present, past1/3 singular, past2 singular/plural, and past participle. Selected mutations eor→ier before 2/3 singular endings follow Cook; forceorfan ier is declared Cook-style normalization of BT cirf/cyrf variants. n+st simplifies to -nst, nn+ð to -nð.
Strong VII lexical pasts hēold and ondrēd are learned with their stems. Dental-ending simplifications in present follow Wright§476; imperative singular drops doubled/final consonant as appropriate.
Strong II bēod/bēad/bud/bod; present2/3 singular bīetst/bīett follows checked Cook§103. Only attested bebēodan prefix identity is licensed.
Lexically attested fordōn and ingān take the checked dōn/gān finite morphology with their prefixes. ingangan/ingangende is a separately supplied lexical variant, not a regular ingān participle.
Selected plain infinitive plus -ne after its final n gives the inflected infinitive -anne/-enne (including -ianne). Promote a prior citation form only through the explicit pair.

lexical_frames.construction: Destroy accusative entity; corresponding patient passive.
Be accustomed to a plain infinitive; controlled subject shared.
Ask an accusative person about a genitive thing, or ask a bounded indirect question; not a double accusative.
Prostrate oneself: accusative reflexive coreferential with subject.
Release an accusative entity; passive uninflected onlīesed with wesan.
Approach a goal marked by tō plus dative.
Entreat accusative person; requested content may be ðæt plus subjunctive.
Cut down an accusative tree/entity.
Place/set accusative entity; corresponding uninflected predicative passive.
Dwell/remain with ordinary static location or no complement.
Overcome/conquer an accusative person or force.
Clothe accusative person with garment marked mid+dative; exact prefixed ge-scrýdan also attested. Passive retains mid+dative.
Fear accusative person/entity, with optional coreferential dative; no forced English-style reflexive.
Destroy accusative entities; plain infinitive after taught modal.
Enter/go in; supplied worthy-content construction takes pres subjunctive ingā. Direction under a roof uses the explicitly supported local prepositional expression.
Send accusative person/entity; corresponding patient passive.
Behold/look at accusative object.
Hate accusative person.
Command dative addressee; ðæt content with subjunctive under the taught command frame, or a licensed relative containing the command.
Return intransitively; explicit route adjunct may specify way.
Lead/bring/take accusative person, optionally with accompanying person (mid+dative) and direction adverb hider.
Speak with a person: mid+dative marks interlocutor. Source141 confirms lexical conversation but its mid+acc is explicitly exceptional and is not generalized.
Pursue/practise accusative study/activity using existing begān finite and imperative systems.
Descend intransitively; of+dative marks source. This is an explicit new sense alongside earlier boarding.
Sell accusative possession (distinct from prior give sense).
Make/do accusative thing; practise an accusative abstract wrongdoing. Distinguish prior physical labour from this transitive scope.
By the same way: ðȳ instrumental determiner plus existing dative-surface ilcan wege in adverbial route function. Reuse dative forms; this does not add an unassigned adjective paradigm.
Pleasant to hear: tō plus inflected infinitive after evaluative adjective, bounded to this expression.
Paired ge ... ge coordinates parallel constituents, both ... and; optional previously supplied ǣgðer requires its explicit support.

Beforan plus accusative in movement/positioning before a person; static dative is a valid alternative construal and not a language error. Cook172 target and prostration frame are considered separately.
Wið plus accusative for static proximity, as stand beside; this accusative does not indicate motion.
Under plus accusative for entering beneath a roof; separate from already taught static under+dative.
Wierðe worthy with ðæt plus present subjunctive for the proposed entry; bounded adjective-content frame corroborated by exact primary roof-entry example.
Indefinite hwilc any in any wonder and if any person; distinguish interrogative which.
Do well to a dative person: extend the prior beneficiary frame to wel plus dōn without expressed deed object.
Sing accusative song, a bounded cognate-object extension.

limits: Only the actual twelve-unit baseline establishes prior teaching.
Clause order is taught as evidenced tendencies, with constituent counting and pronoun exceptions; Cook25.7 retains its own explicit verb-last target.
Reference can remain ambiguous; no nearest-noun or exclusively human masculine-pronoun rule is taught.
Complete morphology assigns only its stated senses, numbers, moods and ordinary uses.
Exact source and Cook aids remain visible during supported tasks and never become unaided-recall requirements.
Existing register surfaces, analyses and histories remain unchanged; current contextual refinements are separately recorded.
The continuous reading ends at153.9 mid wes; the separately supported source-order fragment does not extend it.
review_independence: The fresh solver receives only the actual learner master, prior accepted units/registers and necessary original page images. Every current audit, proposal, contract analysis and answer-bearing file is withheld until frozen solutions.

principal_parts.scope: All four parts are printed for reference. Explain finite distribution from them; nonfinite citations are supplied.
